$comment: W27e's labelled probe scene matrix — claims §5.133 §7's run, and NOTHING but
`dump-layers` reads this file. It is a SEPARATE spec, run through VITREA_SCENES,
so scenes.json and the frozen bed stay untouched.
WHY IT EXISTS. §5.133 §2: 58 of the 60 committed `vibrantColorMatrix`
occurrences sit on the surface's own highlight layer, 2 on an author tint's
gradient layer, and NONE on a label — because the reference harness renders
`Color.clear` inside every `glassEffect` by rule. So the corpus cannot say
whether Apple installs a vibrancy operator on a LABEL at all, which is the
whole of S284 ('the label automatically becomes vibrant, based on its
textColor') and §5.133 §8 (c), the one thing W27e G1 cannot fit around.
WHY IT BREACHES NOTHING. `dump-layers` reads a Core Animation configuration
and captures no pixels; its own doc comment says so and it writes nothing
under `fixtures/`. Three separate things keep a label away from the bed: no
scene in scenes.json declares one, `capture` refuses a labelled scene in
either pose before it opens a window, and `dump-layers` refuses an --out
inside the fixture directory. The no-text fixture rule is unchanged and
unweakened (SceneViews.swift, rule 2).
WHAT IT COVERS, against §5.133 §7 and §4:
- the THREE BRACKET CELLS at span 44 — impulse (linear 0.003750),
dark-solid (0.011711) and mid-dark-solid (0.059511). Two of the three
carry the dark-glass operator on the highlight and the third does not, so
they are where a label's operator would switch if it switches with the
glass.
- BOTH SIDES OF THE JOINT SELECTOR `backdropToneAdaptation(tone,
sizeThickness(span))`. Above it: the two span-44 dark cells. Below it:
dark-solid at span 96 (same backdrop, same tone, does not switch — the
cell that refutes a tone-only threshold), and checkerboard, light-solid
and photo, which never switch at any span.
- THE SPAN LADDER RE-POINTED AT dark-solid: 44 / 48 / 64 / 80 / 96. §5.133
§4 records that the two candidate selector laws differ only in where
between spans 44 and 96 the switch crosses at a dark backdrop, and that
'the corpus holds no cell there'. These five are that interval. They also
bracket Apple's own `tracksLuma`, which the corpus shows as 1 for every
span ≤ 64 and 0 for every span ≥ 72.
- THE NEW BACKGROUND, `mid-chroma-solid`, with a saturated label beside the
automatic one: the operator's chroma gain is 1.5 on the default and 3.0 on
the dark-glass variant, so a saturated label is where a chroma gain would
be visible in the configuration at all.
- ONE TINTED CELL. §5.133 §9: the author tint does not enter the highlight
operator, and 'whatever W27e publishes for a tinted control's label cannot
cite Apple for it'. Whether it enters a LABEL's operator is unasked.
- A BARE TWIN for every labelled scene, so the label's own layer is
identified by difference against the same cell without it rather than by
recognising a class name.
Run BOTH schemes (`--scheme light`, `--scheme dark`): §5.133 §6 records scheme,
scale and accessibility as fully confounded in the committed corpus — 57 of 57
dumps are light, 1x, standard — so whether the dark scheme carries a third
operator is unanswerable from it.
NOT COVERED: §5.133 §7's fourth solid tone rung strictly between linear 0.0117
and 0.0595. It needs a background that does not exist, and a background needs a
committed raster before the reader can state its tone. The three rungs above
are the declared bracket's own ends (0.011711, 0.059511], which is what the
selector's threshold is bracketed by today.

impulse.$comment: Spec-mandated. A grid of small bright squares on black approximates a 2-D impulse train: the material's response to it IS the blur kernel, and the spacing keeps neighbouring responses from overlapping at any plausible sigma. A literal single pixel is too little energy to measure at 1x.

dark-solid.$comment: System dark. Pairs with the dark-scheme profiles.

$comment: W7's missing holdout backdrop, and the ONLY reason this background exists.
W7's measured tone-adaptation law is a smoothstep DOWN over a curve
argument of backdropLuminance + 0.09*sizeThickness(span), with edges at
0.14 and 0.02 — so the whole axis lives between those two luminances, and
every backdrop the bed already had sits OUTSIDE that band: dark-solid at
linear 0.0117 is below the lower edge (fully adapted), and every other one
— hc-text, checkerboard, photo, light-solid — is above the upper edge
(not adapting at all). The axis therefore landed with a holdout that
proves no regression and cannot validate the mechanism (W7 Surprise,
2026-08-30: 'a bed gap, not a discipline breach').
Measured, not asserted. Each committed 1x raster's linear-light mean by
Rec.709 — the same rule the runtime samples a backdrop with — evaluated
against the landed constants at a capsule-button's 44px span
(sizeThickness = smoothstep(32, 96, 44) = 0.09229, so the size term adds
+0.00831 to the curve's argument):
impulse         0.003750  ->  1.000000   pinned at the ceiling
dark-solid      0.011711  ->  0.999999   pinned at the ceiling
mid-dark-solid  0.059511  ->  0.650196   ON THE SLOPE
photo           0.214065  ->  0.000000   off the curve
checkerboard    0.500000  ->  0.000000   off the curve
hc-text         0.740031  ->  0.000000   off the curve
light-solid     0.890969  ->  0.000000   off the curve
For a capsule the curve saturates at 1 at or below linear 0.011694 and
reaches 0 at or above 0.131694. Every backdrop the bed had was outside
that window, so every dark cell was pinned flat against a rail and
carried no gradient at all: a refit could reshape the curve freely
without moving a single committed pixel. That is the gap, measured, and
mid-dark-solid at 0.650196 is the one point on the slope that closes it.
A neutral 69/255 grey is linear 0.059511 by Rec.709 — squarely inside the
transition, and far enough from both edges that the size term (up to
+0.09 for a maximally thick span) cannot push it out of the band. Neutral
rather than tinted on purpose: the axis is a function of LUMINANCE, so a
chromatic backdrop would confound the one thing this scene measures.
W27c G1b's missing chroma anchor, and the ONLY reason this background
exists. Same argument, same shape, as mid-dark-solid above: an axis the
bed identifies only where it cannot be isolated, and one purpose-built
uniform patch that puts a point on it.
The axis is CHROMA TRANSFER — how much of a backdrop's colour the
material transmits. Claims §5.134 §3 (c)/(e) classify the inactive
endpoint's two colour residuals as one model-form gap: the reference's
inactive material transmits MORE of a chromatic backdrop's chroma than
its active one, rising with span, and the one declared field that governs
chroma transmission is the body lerp's alpha, which neither scheme's
recede moves. Every chroma observation in the bed today comes from
`photo`, a broadband field whose chroma, luminance and spatial structure
all vary together — so a chroma error there is confounded with a level
error and with the far-span scatter residual at the same time. Every
backdrop that is uniform (light-solid, dark-solid, mid-dark-solid) is
NEUTRAL. The bed therefore has no cell at which transmitted chroma can be
read on its own, and experiment arm A1's (level, chroma) reachability
test is an inference rather than a measurement.
Measured, not asserted. The level is matched to `photo` so that level and
chroma vary independently across the pair, and the hue and saturation are
chosen to be the most chroma sRGB can carry at that level:
photo@1x, mean linear Rec.709 over the canvas   0.214065
OKLab chroma                                    0.3089
OKLab hue                                       318.7 deg
(213, 2, 255) is the integer sRGB triple of greatest OKLab chroma whose
luminance is within 5e-4 of photo's, searched over the whole cube. A
zero-variance backdrop at photo's own level means the untinted pair
photo/mid-chroma-solid differs in chroma and spatial structure and NOT in
level, which is what makes transmitted chroma separable from the level
target the recede actually moves.
The hue is 318.7 deg and systemOrange's is 62.6 deg — 104 deg apart in
OKLab, the widest practical separation at this level. That is deliberate:
the tinted cell here has to separate 'the author's hue survives' from
'the backdrop's chroma is transmitted', which claims §5.134 §3 (e) shows
the checkerboard could not, and a backdrop sharing the tint's hue would
confound exactly those two.
Not a substitute for photo. A saturated patch is where the transfer is
READ; photo is where it has to hold with structure present.

checkerboard.$comment: Spec-mandated. Every cell edge is a step edge, so one capture yields many edge-spread samples for blur system identification.

light-solid.$comment: System light grey. The flat case: no backdrop detail, so tint and rim read alone.

photo.$comment: A deterministic multi-frequency colour field rather than a real photograph: it carries broadband detail and saturated hue transitions (what a photo contributes to a glass diff) with no licensed asset and no decode differences between the two renderers.

capsule-button.$comment: The canonical control. Capsules are exact in vitrea's field family (S2), so this scene isolates material error from corner error.

orange.$comment: systemOrange. Warm, far from the material's neutral white, and the hue Apple's own tinting examples use.

profiles.$comment: Present only so `dump-layers` can resolve a colour scheme. No profile here is ever captured: every scene declares a label or is the bare twin of one, and `capture` refuses the whole file.

$comment: Every scene is `recorded`: captured and committed and read by nothing — no fit,
no self-check, no bound and no claim may cite a pixel of it. Nothing here is
ever captured in the first place, and the role is what says so mechanically
rather than in prose. `validate()` requires every scene to hold one.
